rows.subtype: Catching the mood of a parent [Receiver]
rows.description: A child senses a parent's tension before a family event and becomes clingy and tearful, though nothing was said. Children pick up the mood of caregivers and can take it as their own.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Laughter and panic in a class [Actor]
rows.description: A giggle spreads through a classroom until nobody can stop, or a rumour of an exam change spreads worry through everyone. Feelings move through groups faster than facts.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Absorbing the crowd's excitement or fear [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager at a match, concert or rally is swept up in the crowd's energy, feeling joy or anger that is not entirely their own. Shared feeling can be warm and can make them act unusually.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26
related mind states: joy, anger, fear, excitement

rows.subtype: Setting the tone of a team [Response]
rows.description: A young team lead notices that their own stress and irritation spread to others, and takes a breath before meetings, speaks calmly and acknowledges pressure honestly. A steady person in the room can settle the group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: anger, calm, relief from stress

rows.subtype: Being known as fair or a cheat [Actor]
rows.description: A child who keeps promises in marbles or card games is invited to play again, while one who cheats is quietly dropped. Children begin to learn that a reputation forms quickly and lasts.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager shares a minor secret with a new friend to see whether it stays private before sharing more. Trust is built in steps, and a single breach is remembered for a long time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who lent money or shared a draft with someone who did not return or misused it feels betrayed and gullible. They learn to trust more carefully rather than to trust nobody.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional hears colleagues discuss who can be relied on and who cannot, before ever working with them. They realise that reputation is gathered through small consistent actions and passed on informally.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person who let others down admits it plainly, makes amends, and then behaves reliably over a long stretch without demanding quick forgiveness. Trust returns slowly through repeated evidence, not through apology alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
